reflexion_entries_to_archive.text: castleBank.test.ts's `expect(CASTLE_BANK_CAP).toBe(5)` DID work — it went red the instant the cap moved and forced the recipe table to be re-read, which is exactly what B4b asks for. But four copies of PROTOCOL_VERSION pinned the same way had all drifted, and every one of their TITLES said 'is 17' while asserting 18. A pinned value only ever says 'someone changed this'; it cannot say what the number is FOR, and it must be hand-edited on every legitimate change. S140 replaced the cap pin with relationship invariants (cap >= HELGA_SIZE, cap >= TURRET_SIZE, cap < VOLTKIN_SIZE, cap < NONET_SHAPE_COUNT) and collapsed four version pins to ONE deliberate one. Keep exactly one pin whose job is 'was this a decision?', and bind everything else to the constant.

All five S140 seats rejected the laserTurret 8->7 retune, and their strongest argument was that step one of implementing it is DELETING codexPresentation.test.ts's anti-drift test — the guard that exists to stop the emblem and the predicate disagreeing about seven. The owner ruled for the retune anyway. The right execution was not to delete the guard but to REBIND it: it now reads TURRET_HUB_DEGREE instead of a literal, so it survives any future retune and is strictly stronger than the version it replaced. A rejected-but-ruled change is an instruction to find the version of it that keeps the protection.

laserTurret's predicate uses `!==` with no upper tolerance, and the host re-validates every 30 ticks. So after the 8->7 retune, a player following any surviving 'seven' copy would build a turret and watch REMOVE_DEFENDER kill it 0.5 s later — 'builds at six, dies at seven'. That reframes a copy migration from cosmetic to load-bearing: the retune is not a constant change with docs to follow, it is a copy migration that happens to include a constant. Added a test asserting NO player-visible 'seven' survives, and a witness test that a 7-leaf star is now rejected.

Both the session brief and one Council seat treated 'cap 7 ships 1 dead box' as a real cost, and Gemini used it as its main argument for cap 8 over 7. It was false: a dead box only exists if you assume a FIXED rectangular grid. Centring each row on its own occupancy gives cap 7 a 4-slot row above a 3-slot row — seven boxes, zero dead, verified exhaustively over cap 1..500. A constraint introduced by a candidate implementation was being priced as a constraint of the problem. Check whether the cost you are weighing belongs to the domain or to your first sketch of the solution.

The bank strip's width was a function of the cap (cap*40 + (cap-1)*6) with no upper bound, so cap 7 put slot 0 at x=-24, hanging off a 268px plate — and castlePanel.test.ts had ZERO bank coverage, so it would have shipped green. Inverting the dependency (slots-per-row DERIVED from the panel width) makes overflow structurally impossible at any cap AND yields exactly the shipped layout at cap 5 — which let the regrid ship and be verified BEFORE the cap moved, separating a risky change into two provable ones. Also kept a witness test that reproduces the old arithmetic and shows it violating the new invariant: prove the guard, don't read it.

I reported to the owner that LOCKED_DECISIONS §7 said the carve-down threshold was already crossed at cap 5, which would have made the whole B4b objection moot. The PRIME-AUDIT caught that §7 is the OUTLIER: BACKLOG B4 and constants.ts both say '>= the biggest recipe'. §7 was a compressed misstatement, and the Council's synthesis had leaned on it AND proposed logging it as 'spent' — ratifying an error into the second-highest-authority document. Corrected §7 instead of retiring it. When three sources disagree, the one that makes your argument easiest is the one to re-read first.

R3_goblin_model.verbatim: goblin tower needs primitives to keep spawning goblins. each 3 primitives dragged into the melee or ranged goblin tower creates one goblin. the primitives are puled from the castle space when the gatherer gathers them. each player starts with one goblin of every kind that either attack the closest enemy structure or each other. takes them 6 attacks to destroy a connector or a UNIT
R3_goblin_model.reading: This REPLACES the amendment's model entirely. The three units are no longer three recipe-anchored DefenderKinds. The new model is a PRODUCER/UNIT split: (a) TWO goblin TOWERS (melee + ranged) are emplacements built from small recipes; (b) feeding a tower 3 primitives produces ONE goblin UNIT; (c) primitives come from the castle bank via the shipped PULL_FROM_BANK -> porch -> place path; (d) goblin UNITS walk out and attack the nearest enemy structure, or each other; (e) 6 attacks destroys a connector (bond) or a unit; (f) every player is granted one goblin of each kind free at match start.
R3_goblin_model.consequence_dissolved: Amendment 2b Q3 (does defender death raze its anchor - wrong for a unit?) is DISSOLVED, not answered. Under the producer model the goblin is not anchored to a recipe primitive at all: the TOWER owns the anchor, the UNIT is spawned. So there is no anchor to raze when a unit dies, and no immortal-defender re-mint risk for units. The re-mint concern now applies only to the towers, where razing the anchor is the correct shipped behaviour anyway.
R3_goblin_model.consequence_substrate: CANDIDATE SUBSTRATE SHIFT, being verified in A.0b before any design rests on it: units look like CREATURES, not Defenders. Creatures already spawn from spawners, walk, carry targetBondId AND targetCreatureId as parallel nullable fields, have hp, and already destroy bonds via chewProgress against CHEW_HITS=5 (owner says 6). Towers look like creatureSpawners. If that holds, the redesign rides shipped machinery instead of extending the defender FSM - and the A.0 finding that new DefenderKinds silently render as nothing and silently drift (neither pinned nor frozen) stops applying to the units.
R3_goblin_model.open_cost: 6 attacks needs a home: A.0b must establish whether chewProgress is strictly per-attacker (so two goblins on one bond do not share progress) or whether the counter must move onto the bond.

R4_stink_tower.verbatim: the tower throws bags in a short range around it. bags of poop cannot damage its own towers only attacks from enemy units can. tower is pretty fragile (has as much hp as 3 connected shapes on a built primitive structure). the tower has 5 bags that he throws - one every 30 sec, once they are all depleted the tower stands there and stinks an area around him and pulls aggro like a bag would asking for enemies to attack h9im and dealing damage when exploding./ if someone destroys the tower while having more bags on him he will deal more damage with a bigger cooler explosion of shit! ;ets make it super creative and epic!!!!!!!
R4_stink_tower.reading: BAGS ARE AMMO, NOT DESTRUCTIBLE PARTS. Five bags, thrown one every 30 s at short range. Bags cannot damage the owner's own towers - only enemy-unit attacks hurt the tower. Tower HP = 3 connected shapes = 3 * PRIMITIVE_MAX_HP = 3000 (coincides exactly with the existing TURRET_DEFENDER_MAX_HP). Once all 5 bags are spent the tower switches to a passive stink AURA and PULLS AGGRO, inviting attackers, and still deals damage when it explodes. DEATH BLAST SCALES WITH BAGS REMAINING - destroying a loaded tower is punished with a bigger explosion. Owner explicitly asked for this to be creative and epic.
R4_stink_tower.consequence_dissolved: Amendment 2b Q2 (AoE hits all 5 bags at once so the tower absorbs 5x the AoE damage - feature or per-structure cap?) is DISSOLVED, not answered. Bags are ammo, so there are no 5 hp-bearing primitives to splash. No per-bag entity family, no untargetable-core mechanic, no per-structure damage cap. This is materially CHEAPER than the amendment 4b B spec it replaces.
R4_stink_tower.consequence_design: The escalating death blast creates a real decision the original spec lacked: rush it while loaded and eat the blast, or wait it out while it throws at you. Also note this INVERTS the amendment's aura model: the aura is now the DEPLETED state (a fallback), not the tower's primary mechanic.
R4_stink_tower.friendly_fire_delta: Amendment 4b table said the death burst hits EVERYONE including the owner's own troops. The new ruling says bags cannot damage the owner's own TOWERS.
